harmony-techniques.name: First inversion for a stepwise bass
harmony-techniques.summary: Place the chord's third in the Bass while the Pad retains the chord identity.
harmony-techniques.useWhen: A short G–F#–E bass descent connects the same chords more smoothly than root jumps.
harmony-techniques.caution: Check which note the Bass actually plays; changing the Pad alone does not change the inversion if the Bass still plays the root.

harmony-techniques.name: Cadential six-four
harmony-techniques.summary: Keep the dominant bass under a second-inversion tonic triad and resolve its upper voices into the dominant before the final tonic.
harmony-techniques.useWhen: A tonal cadence needs a brief suspended sound before the dominant resolves.
harmony-techniques.caution: The cadential context matters: do not treat every second-inversion chord as a dominant or an interchangeable sus chord.
